podcast.title: "Black Paramore" Analogy
podcast.body: Meet Me @ The Altar is likened to a "black version of Paramore," suggesting a similar pop punk style but with a distinct identity. "Meet me at the altar is like a block version of Paramore, except that they're all women and LGBTQ+."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: All-Women and LGBTQ+ Lineup
podcast.body: The band is composed entirely of women and identifies as LGBTQ+, contributing to their unique identity within the pop punk scene. "except that they're all women and LGBTQ+. They're an excellent pop punk band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Important Black Inclusive Alt-Rock Group
podcast.body: Meet Me @ The Altar is mentioned as a Black inclusive group making important contributions to alternative rock. "meet me at the altar..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Remote Collaboration Model
podcast.body: The members of Meet Me @ The Altar typically reside in three different states—Florida, Georgia, and New Jersey—and collaboratively create their songs online. "Most of the time the members are in three different states, Florida, Georgia, New Jersey, and they all collaborate on songs online."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
